title: Syntra plugin manifest
description: Describes a plugin process the Syntra daemon can supervise. The daemon discovers plugins by reading these manifests, so anything a user should see about a plugin belongs here rather than in the daemon.

description.description: One or two sentences describing the capability this plugin adds, shown in the plugin manager.

author.description: Person or organisation responsible for the plugin.

source.description: Where the source code lives, so a user can audit a plugin before trusting it with clipboard contents.

bundled.description: True for plugins shipped with Syntra. Bundled plugins are updated with the application and cannot be uninstalled from the plugin manager.

on_demand.description: True when the daemon starts this plugin only for the duration of a task rather than keeping it running. Such a plugin is reported as available rather than stopped when idle, because not running is its normal state.

capabilities.description: What the plugin does. A clipboard or transfer plugin declares the clipboard fields and at least one MIME type. A plugin that only reacts to the pointer declares `pointer_events` and none of those.

pointer_events.description: True when the plugin wants to be told as a pointer enters, leaves or pushes against a screen edge. The daemon then launches it, sends it its settings after the handshake, and forwards those events. Such a plugin only listens; anything it sends other than an error report stops it.

settings.description: What the user can change. The plugin manager draws a control for each, stores the choice per plugin, and hands the current values to the plugin after its handshake and whenever one changes.

key.description: Name the plugin receives the value under.

default.description: Value until the user chooses one, written as the wire form: `true` or `false`, an option value, a number, or `#rrggbb`.
